reportTitle: Research Report: Main Causes of Climate Change
researchQuestion: What are the main causes of climate change?
keyFindings: Fossil fuel combustion accounts for 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions (36-37 billion tonnes CO2/year)
Agricultural emissions contribute significantly through methane from livestock (90-100 Mt/year) and nitrous oxide from fertilizers (4-6 Mt/year)
Deforestation releases 4-5 billion tonnes CO2/year while eliminating critical carbon sinks
Industrial process emissions from cement (2.8 Gt CO2/year) and steel involve chemical reactions independent of energy source
Methane leakage from fossil fuel infrastructure (70-90 Mt/year) is 25-40% higher than industry reporting
Transportation sector contributes 8 billion tonnes CO2/year with aviation and shipping presenting unique decarbonization challenges
Climate feedback mechanisms (permafrost thawing, ice-albedo feedback) are amplifying warming with potential for 0.2-0.4°C additional warming by 2100
Non-CO2 gases (methane, nitrous oxide, fluorinated gases) contribute 25-30% of radiative forcing
crossCuttingInsights: Fossil fuel system dominance makes energy transformation the single most critical intervention point
Non-CO2 gases offer near-term climate benefits due to shorter atmospheric lifetimes
Feedback mechanisms are transitioning from theoretical concerns to active amplifiers
Process emissions require technological innovation beyond renewable energy adoption
Sectoral interconnections require systems-level solutions rather than isolated interventions
remainingQuestions: Precise quantification of permafrost carbon release timing and magnitude
Reconciliation of satellite vs bottom-up methane emission measurements
Tipping point thresholds for major Earth systems
Regional variations in Amazon carbon balance
Aerosol cooling effects and implications of air quality improvements
